newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait sells shares in local securities firm.
newsitem.headline: Kuwait sells shares in local securities firm.

text.p: Kuwait has sold 24 percent of its 330 million shares in Securities Group to private investors for 22.4 million dinars ($75 million) by public auction, newspapers reported on Monday.
The sale was part of Kuwait's plan to shed state holdings in about 60 local firms and public services such as electricity, water and telecommunications, officials said.
The Sunday auction of 80 million Securities Group shares closed at 280 fils. The starting price was 136 fils.
There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
Securities Group is not listed on the Kuwait Stock Exchange.
The privatisation plan, announced after the 1991 Gulf War, is supervised by the state's investment arm, Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA).

The newspapers also reported that KIA plans to sell another 220 million Securities Group shares, 66.6 percent of the government's holdings in the brokerage and investment firm, by public subscription at a yet to be decided price.
